gaps.sentence: ___ time I visit Rome, I discover something new.
gaps.explanation: 'Every time I ...' introduces repeated occasions; 'all time' and 'whole time' are not used here.

gaps.sentence: We had a ___ of fun at the fair.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of fun' is the fixed phrase; 'fun' is uncountable and the article 'a' forces 'lot'.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ in a bad mood.
gaps.explanation: 'Mostly' is an adverb meaning mainly or usually; 'most' as a quantifier needs a noun.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ came to the afternoon lecture.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly anyone' is already negative — do not add 'no one'.

gaps.sentence: She spent a great ___ of time preparing the report.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: a great ___ of + uncountable
gaps.explanation: 'A great deal of time' is used with uncountable nouns; 'a great number of' needs a countable plural.

gaps.sentence: We see our grandparents ___ other weekend.
gaps.explanation: 'Every other weekend' means alternate weekends; 'each other' has a different, reciprocal meaning.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the two proposals has been approved so far.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two' — 'none' is for three or more.
'Too cold to swim' means the temperature prevents swimming; 'enough' would follow the adjective.
